# Easywurld — 30-day calendar: 11 posts and 2 stories a day

**Monday 2 November–Tuesday 1 December 2026 · Africa/Lagos (WAT, UTC+1)**

**330 core posts · 60 stories · 210 LinkedIn posts · 1380 platform placements.**

## Strategy before production


**Active campaign:** Monday 2 November–Tuesday 1 December 2026
**Platforms:** TikTok, Instagram and Facebook, plus LinkedIn for siphoned posts
**Volume:** 11 content posts + 2 stories per day on TikTok, Instagram and Facebook = 39 scheduled placements per day, plus 26 LinkedIn posts across the month. **1,196 placements in total.**
**Timezone:** Africa/Lagos (WAT, UTC+1)

This replaces the 22-post weekday plan. The owner wants a high-volume, series-led channel. The strategy below keeps that volume but makes it repeatable, recognisable and reviewable.

## 1. Is the idea good?

Yes — the series structure is the strongest part. It gives people recurring reasons to follow: niche ideas, myth-checking, trend analysis, AI workflows, humour, offer education, copywriting lessons and a daily introduction to Easywurld.

The risk is not the number 10. The risk is publishing 10 versions of the same generic tip, or 10 hard sells, every day. We avoid that by giving each slot a distinct job, rotating the offer, varying the format, and adapting the copy to each platform.

**Rule:** 10 core ideas per day, not 30 separate ideas. Each idea is produced once and adapted for TikTok, Instagram and Facebook. That is 30 placements, but one production system.

## 2. Positioning

> Easywurld helps small businesses make the message, website, content and follow-up work together.

**Audience:** owner-led small businesses in Lagos and across Nigeria.
**Business objective:** relevant WhatsApp enquiries, well-matched DIY pack sales, and scoped project briefs.
**Voice:** plain, specific, useful, slightly witty. No fake client results, no inflated marketing promises.

The account should feel like a useful marketing studio thinking out loud: here is what we would post, here is what we would question, here is what we would automate, here is what we would steal from great copywriters, and here is who we are.

## 3. The 10 daily series

| Slot | Time | Series | Job | Default format |
|---:|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 07:00 | **If I ran this account** | Show niche-specific social media thinking | Talking head + carousel |
| 2 | 08:30 | **Marketing Myth Court** | Debunk or qualify common marketing advice | Talking head |
| 3 | 10:00 | **Trend Desk** | What is trending / what trended last week, and whether a business should use it | Screen recap / talking head |
| 4 | 11:30 | **AI Automation Build** | One practical AI or automation workflow | Screen demo / workflow carousel |
| 5 | 13:00 | **Meme: owner life** | Relatable small-business humour | Original static / short video |
| 6 | 14:30 | **Offer Spotlight A** | Problem + what the pack actually contains | Carousel / talking head |
| 7 | 16:00 | **Steal This Copy Move** | Break down a copywriting expert’s principle and apply it | Carousel / talking head |
| 8 | 17:30 | **Meme: marketing / AI / clients** | Relatable industry humour | Original static / short video |
| 9 | 19:00 | **Offer Spotlight B** | Objection, limitation or next step for the same daily offer | Talking head / static |
| 10 | 20:30 | **Meet Easywurld** | A new angle on who we are, what we do and who we serve | Rotating format |
| 11 | 22:00 | **One Last Thought** | The Operator closes the day with one calm, certain line | Faceless AI talking head |

Platform offset: TikTok at the slot time, Instagram +10 minutes, Facebook +20 minutes. These are starting test times, not proven best times.

### The two daily stories

| Slot | Time | Type | Job |
|---|---|---|---|
| A | 12:30 | **Poll / quiz** | One tap. A question the audience can answer in a second, with the answer revealed on frame three |
| B | 21:00 | **Behind the desk** | The Operator's desk, then tomorrow's 07:00 hook, then a link sticker |

Instagram at the slot time, Facebook +5 minutes, TikTok +10 minutes. Fifteen seconds each, captions burned in, three frames, one sticker.

### LinkedIn pulls

LinkedIn is not a fourth version of the same daily post. Six posts a week are siphoned from work that already exists: Monday a carousel write-up as a document post, Tuesday a teach post, Wednesday a show post, Thursday a trust post, Friday the week's best vertical video, Saturday an offer lesson. Thursday and Friday are the strongest reading days; Sunday stays quiet.

### Story 11 — One Last Thought

> The persona is defined in [AVATAR_OPERATOR.md](./AVATAR_OPERATOR.md).

A faceless, unhurried voice at 22:00. One flat sentence, one turn, one line worth repeating, one ask. The face is never shown; the night desk, the notebook and the voice carry the identity. It exists to make the account feel like a person with a point of view rather than a queue of posts, and to build a fixed evening habit. Everything about it is disclosed: `AI presenter · Easywurld`.

### Series 1 — If I ran this account

Prompt: “If I was managing social media for a [niche] in Lagos, this is what I would post this week.”

Each episode gives three post ideas, one mistake to avoid and one first action. Rotate niches: fashion, food, beauty, fitness, property, education, events, logistics, retail, services. Do not pretend Easywurld manages these accounts. Say “if I ran” or “here is the plan I would test.”

### Series 2 — Marketing Myth Court

Prompt: “Marketing myth: [claim]. Verdict: [true / false / it depends]. Here is the test.”

Do not debunk with another absolute. Use verdicts: mostly false, partly true, depends on the goal. Give a small test the owner can run. Examples: “post every day”, “hashtags are dead”, “you need a website before content”, “AI can replace strategy”, “more followers means more sales”.

### Series 3 — Trend Desk

Prompt: “This week’s trend watch: [format]. Should a small business use it? Here is the Easywurld adaptation.”

Trend posts must be verified before recording. Use TikTok Creative Center, Instagram Reels feed, platform newsrooms and dated trend reports. Save the source URL, date checked and example link in the production sheet. Do not invent a trend or use an unlicensed song because it is trending.

For launch week, candidate formats reported in late October 2026 include Brand Vibe, Pick Your Emoji, Gold Star Behavior, interface-as-content and short proof Reels. These are candidates, not guaranteed current trends. Recheck on 1 November. [2](https://drizzledigital.com/social-media-trends-oct-2026/) [1](https://lightreel.ai/blogs/whats-trending-on-instagram) [5](https://www.socialpilot.co/blog/instagram-reels-trends)

### Series 4 — AI Automation Build

Prompt: “One AI workflow a small business can test: [workflow]. Input → AI draft → human check → next action.”

Show the boundary. AI can draft, classify, summarise or prepare. A human approves prices, promises, legal/health/finance answers and customer-sensitive replies. Use real screen recordings or clearly labelled concept demos. Do not imply a workflow is live if it is a sample.

### Series 5 and 8 — Two memes

One owner-life meme and one marketing/AI/client meme per day. **Scene-led, not a wall of text:** a real photograph of the moment (the empty plastic chairs, the face-down phone, the blank screen), with a small two-line caption in the lower third. Eight scene plates are supplied in `marketing/assets/meme-scenes/`. No stolen meme templates with unclear rights, no fake customer screenshots, no punching down at customers. The caption under the post carries the useful lesson.

### Series 6 and 9 — Two offer posts, one daily offer

Feature one offer per day. Post A explains the problem and contents. Post B handles an objection, limitation or next step. Rotate the nine packs. Do not sell nine packs in one day.

Current source price: ₦5,000 per DIY pack. Confirm price, contents, payment and delivery before publishing. State what the pack does not do. Custom projects are separate.

### Series 7 — Steal This Copy Move

Prompt: “Steal this copy move from [expert]: [principle]. Don’t steal their words. Steal the structure. Here is an original Easywurld example.”

Break down the technique, not long copyrighted ads. Use short examples, attribute the source, and create a new Lagos/small-business example. Rotate Ogilvy, Schwartz, Sugarman, Halbert, Hopkins, Caples, Wiebe, Harry Dry and others. Marketing Examples and Copyhackers are useful modern reference points. [1](https://marketingexamples.com/) [1](https://copyhackers.com/about-us/)

### Series 10 — Meet Easywurld

A new introduction every day, not the same bio repeated. Rotate: who we serve, what we do, how we work, what we don’t do, sample tour, process, AI policy, handover, pricing philosophy, how to brief us, what happens after you message, why we label samples, and what we are building.

## 4. Format mix

The series are the structure; the format changes inside them.

- AI talking head: myth verdicts, offer objections, and the 22:00 Operator close.
- Screen demo: AI workflows, trend recaps, sample tours.
- Carousel: niche plans, checklists, offer contents, copy breakdowns.
- Scene-led static meme: the two daily meme slots.
- Story frames: the two daily stories (poll/quiz and behind-the-desk).
- Text post / document: the six weekly LinkedIn pulls.

Do not make every slot a talking head. The feed needs visual variety. The Operator is a production tool and a recognisable voice, not the entire brand.

## 5. Platform adaptation

| Platform | Adaptation |
|---|---|
| TikTok | Native vertical video, spoken hook, fast first frame, captions, one CTA. Static memes can be photo posts or short text videos. |
| Instagram | Reel or carousel depending on the idea. Carousel copy can be more structured. Check crop and safe areas. |
| Facebook | Native text + image/video or carousel. Caption can be slightly more conversational. Do not just paste TikTok text with hashtags. Stories posted +5 minutes after Instagram. |
| LinkedIn | Rewritten from the same idea, never pasted. First line is the whole hook, paragraphs of one or two lines, no hashtag block (two tags maximum), link in the first comment. One document post and one native video a week at most. |

One core idea can have three captions. The hook and CTA stay consistent; the wording and format fit the platform.

## 6. AI talking-head rules

The AI presenter is the **anonymous Operator persona** — faceless founder, night desk, warm lamp, calm low voice. Full persona, delivery card, five scripts, script formula and 30-night arc: [AVATAR_OPERATOR.md](./AVATAR_OPERATOR.md). Scene plates and voice samples: `marketing/assets/avatar/`.

Because no face is shown, no real likeness or photo release is needed. That removes the last blocker on the talking-head slots. Never describe the Operator as the owner's real face, never use the fictional demo founder image, and disclose every clip as `AI presenter · Easywurld`.

TikTok requires disclosure for realistic AI-generated media, including a person portrayed saying something they did not say. Enable the platform AI setting and keep a visible label. [1](https://support.tiktok.com/en/using-tiktok/creating-videos/ai-generated-content)

House style: chest-up, eye-level, natural light, restrained gestures, corrected phrase captions, one useful cutaway, no logo intro, no long end card. CapCut’s guidance supports meaningful jump cuts paired with reframes or cutaways rather than decorative transitions. [1](https://www.capcut.com/create/video-transitions-crossfade-hard-cut-jump-cut)

Use own/licensed audio or TikTok’s Commercial Music Library with the applicable rights. A trending personal-account sound is not automatically cleared for a brand. [1](https://ads.tiktok.com/help/article/how-to-use-the-commercial-music-library)

## 7. Production system for 11 posts and 2 stories a day

Batch by series, not by day.

- **Sunday:** write/verify the week’s 77 core ideas. Record Operator batches by series. Record screen demos. Design memes and carousels from templates. Render the week’s 14 stories and siphon the LinkedIn set.
- **Daily:** assemble the 11 posts and 2 stories, adapt captions, QA, schedule.
- **Weekly:** review series performance, not just individual posts.

Suggested batch blocks:

1. Niche plans: 7 episodes.
2. Myth Court: 7 Operator clips.
3. Trend Desk: research + 7 recaps.
4. AI Build: 7 workflows.
5. Memes: 14 scene-led originals.
6. Offer: one pack, 14 posts.
7. Copy Move: 7 lessons.
8. Meet Easywurld: 7 angles.
9. One Last Thought: 7 Operator closes (batch with slot 2; same voice, same preset).
10. Stories: 14 three-frame sequences.
11. LinkedIn: 6 siphoned posts, written last from the finished copy.

This is heavy. Use templates, one locked Operator voice, caption presets and a shared asset library. If a slot fails QA, hold it rather than publishing unreviewed AI. The volume target stays 11 + 2; quality control is not optional.

## 8. Scheduling

TikTok’s official scheduler announcement describes a 15-minute to 10-day window and says scheduled posts must be deleted and re-uploaded to change them. Check current availability in your account. [1](https://ads.tiktok.com/business/en/blog/introducing-video-scheduler-now-you-can-plan-tiktoks-in-advance)

Meta Business Suite can schedule Facebook and Instagram, but limits and features vary by account and surface. Check the planner in your own account. Do not assume a CSV auto-publishes.

The CSV in this repo is a production/planning sheet. Every row starts Draft. Mark Scheduled only after the platform confirms it. No social account is connected here.

## 9. Measurement

Review by series after 7 days:

- Which series earns saves/shares?
- Which earns watch time/completion?
- Which earns profile visits and WhatsApp keyword enquiries?
- Which offer gets qualified purchases or project briefs?
- Which meme gets shares without attracting the wrong audience?

Keep 11 posts and 2 stories a day for the test, but change hooks, formats and angles based on evidence. Track the 22:00 Operator separately: if watch-through and follows climb during that slot, the persona is the asset, not the frequency. Do not declare a winner from one post. Do not invent month-end results.

## 10. Trust rules

- All portfolio work is concept/sample. Label it.
- No fake testimonials, rankings, client results or campaign metrics.
- Hypothetical businesses/chats are labelled example.
- DIY packs are not custom projects.
- Trend posts need a dated source check.
- Copywriting posts attribute the principle and use original examples.
- AI presenters/voices are disclosed.
- Private CVs, identity sources, customer messages and payment details stay out of public Git.

## 11. Launch gates

- [ ] Confirm handles, website URL, WhatsApp and offer fulfilment.
- [ ] Confirm the Operator persona and locked voice; no real likeness is required.
- [ ] Render the week's story frames and confirm sticker placement in the preview.
- [ ] Verify launch-week trends on 1 November.
- [ ] Produce first 70 core posts / 210 platform adaptations.
- [ ] QA captions, prices, disclosures, crops and audio rights.
- [ ] Schedule only approved assets.
- [ ] Record actual URLs and results afterwards.


## Series playbook


**Active campaign:** 2 November–1 December 2026
**Cadence:** 11 content posts + 2 stories per day, adapted to TikTok, Instagram and Facebook = 39 placements per day, plus 26 LinkedIn posts across the month.

This playbook turns the strategy into repeatable production rules. The canonical editorial source is `marketing/series-plan.json`. The expanded machine-readable plan is `marketing/content-plan.json`.

## 1. Daily slot map

| Slot | WAT | Series | Core format | Job |
|---:|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | 07:00 | If I ran this account | Carousel | Niche-specific posting plan |
| 2 | 08:30 | Marketing Myth Court | AI talking head | Verdict + small test |
| 3 | 10:00 | Trend Desk | Screen demo | Dated trend teardown + verification gate |
| 4 | 11:30 | AI Automation Build | Screen demo or carousel | One bounded workflow |
| 5 | 13:00 | Meme: owner life | Original static | Recognition humour |
| 6 | 14:30 | Offer Spotlight A | Carousel | Problem + actual contents |
| 7 | 16:00 | Steal This Copy Move | Carousel | Attributed principle + original example |
| 8 | 17:30 | Meme: marketing / AI / clients | Original static | Industry humour |
| 9 | 19:00 | Offer Spotlight B | AI talking head | Objection / limitation |
| 10 | 20:30 | Meet Easywurld | Rotating | New introduction angle/format |
| 11 | 22:00 | One Last Thought | AI talking head (faceless Operator) | One calm, certain line to close the day |

Platform offsets: TikTok +0, Instagram +10, Facebook +20 minutes. These are test times, not proven best times.

**Stories:** A at 12:30 (poll/quiz, 3 frames) and B at 21:00 (behind the desk, 3 frames). Instagram at the slot time, Facebook +5, TikTok +10.

**LinkedIn:** six pulled posts a week at 09:00 — Monday document/carousel write-up, Tuesday teach, Wednesday show, Thursday trust, Friday native video, Saturday offer lesson.

## 2. Series rules

### If I ran this account

- Say “If I ran” or “I would test.” Do not imply Easywurld manages the business.
- Give three post ideas, one mistake and one first action.
- Use Lagos/Nigeria context where relevant, but do not invent local facts.
- Label hypothetical businesses, prices and chats as examples.

### Marketing Myth Court

- Use a verdict: true, mostly false, partly true, false, or it depends.
- Do not replace one absolute with another.
- Give a small test the owner can run.
- Do not claim platform rules without a current source.

### Trend Desk

Trend posts are **held** until the verification log is complete.

1. Check the dated source already attached to the brief.
2. Within seven days before publishing, find a current public example on the target platform.
3. Record the example URL, platform, date checked, rights check, relevance note and reviewer in `marketing/TREND_VERIFICATION.csv`.
4. If the format is still relevant and rights are clear, update the script to say “this week” or “last week” only when the evidence supports it.
5. If no current example is verified, publish only as a dated teardown: “Reported on [date]. Here is the structure.” Remove live-trend wording.

Late-October 2026 candidate formats include Brand Vibe, Pick Your Emoji, Gold Star Behavior, short proof Reels, native-interface tutorials and comment-keyword DM flows. These are candidates, not guaranteed November trends. [1](https://drizzledigital.com/social-media-trends-oct-2026/) [2](https://socialbee.com/blog/latest-instagram-trends/) [1](https://lightreel.ai/blogs/whats-trending-on-instagram)

Do not use a trending personal-account sound for a brand unless the rights are cleared. TikTok Business Accounts should use the Commercial Music Library or separately licensed audio. [2](https://ads.tiktok.com/help/article/how-to-use-the-commercial-music-library)

### AI Automation Build

- Show one workflow: input → AI draft → human check → output.
- State what is not automated.
- Use anonymised or fictional input.
- Keep prices, promises, legal/medical/financial answers and complaints behind human review.
- If using a repo demo, label it concept/sample. Do not imply it sent real messages or produced live results.

### Memes

- Two per day: one owner-life, one marketing/AI/client.
- Original text-led graphics or short text videos.
- Joke about the work, not the customer.
- No fake notifications, stolen templates, private screenshots or punching down.
- The caption carries the useful lesson.

### Offer Spotlight A and B

- One featured offer per day.
- Post A: problem + actual contents + price + DIY boundary.
- Post B: one objection or limitation + direct answer + same keyword CTA.
- Rotate the nine packs. Do not sell all nine in one day.
- Confirm price, contents, payment and delivery before publishing.
- No guaranteed results, fake scarcity or invented testimonials.

### Steal This Copy Move

- Attribute the principle to the expert and source.
- Steal the structure, not long copyrighted copy.
- Use an original Easywurld/Lagos example.
- Do not imply the expert endorses Easywurld.

Rotation: David Ogilvy, Eugene Schwartz, Joe Sugarman, Gary Halbert, Claude Hopkins, John Caples, Joanna Wiebe, Harry Dry, Ann Handley, Robert Bly.

Reference points: Ogilvy on research and headlines; Schwartz on existing desire and awareness; Sugarman on reading momentum; Halbert on market and offer; Hopkins on testing; Caples on self-interest headlines; Wiebe on voice-of-customer; Dry on concrete, checkable copy; Handley on utility and voice; Bly on benefits and clear CTAs. [1](https://copywarfare.com/greatest-copywriters/) [1](https://copyhackers.com/about-us/) [2](https://copyhackers.com/join-the-conversation-customer/) [1](https://marketingexamples.com/copywriting) [1](https://www.shortform.com/blog/everybody-writes-by-ann-handley/) [1](https://www.goodreads.com/book/show/162340.The_Copywriter_s_Handbook)

### Meet Easywurld

- A new angle and format each day.
- Rotate: studio map, one-sentence studio, process, sample labels, service menu, FAQ, AI policy, handover, pricing boundary, brief template, contact route, audience map, sample tour, series map, website anatomy, follow-up flow, local checklist, proposal anatomy, message worksheet, launch checklist, tool stack, behind the calendar, homepage tour, boundaries, who we serve, how to start, review rhythm, invitation, dictionary.
- Do not invent team size, office, clients or results.
- Do not use the fictional demo founder as the owner.

### One Last Thought (22:00, the Operator)

- One flat sentence, one turn, one line worth repeating, one ask. 18–24 seconds.
- No greeting, no logo at the open, no shouting, no urgency. The face is never visible.
- Same voice, same preset, same frame every night. The repetition is the brand.
- Never invent a story about the owner. Lines about the work are safe; lines about a lived event need confirmation.
- Full persona and scripts: [AVATAR_OPERATOR.md](./AVATAR_OPERATOR.md).

### Story A — Poll / quiz (12:30)

- Frame 1: the question. Frame 2: two options. Frame 3: the answer plus one sentence of reasoning.
- One tap only. No link on a poll story. The point is a signal and a habit, not a sale.
- Never write a question whose answer shames the audience.

### Story B — Behind the desk (21:00)

- Frame 1: the desk scene. Frame 2: tomorrow's 07:00 hook. Frame 3: link sticker to the site or the lead post.
- It teases tomorrow's work; it never sells directly.
- If tomorrow's post is a held Trend Desk, do not tease a live-trend claim.

### LinkedIn pulls

- Six a week, siphoned from work that already exists. Never paste a TikTok caption.
- First line carries the whole hook. Paragraphs of one or two lines. Two tags maximum. Link in the first comment.
- Monday's document post and Friday's video are the only heavy assets; the rest are text.
- Thursday and Friday are the reading days; Sunday stays quiet.

## 5. Weekly batch rhythm

Each week produces 70 core posts and 210 platform placements.

| Block | Weekly output | Notes |
|---|---:|---|
| Niche plans | 7 carousels | Batch by niche; use owned/labelled visuals |
| Myth Court | 7 talking heads | Record in one avatar/voice session |
| Trend Desk | 7 teardowns | Research first; hold until verified |
| AI Build | 7 workflows | Record real demos or set workflow cards |
| Memes | 14 originals | Design from one template system |
| Offer | 14 posts | One pack, two angles per day |
| Copy Move | 7 breakdowns | Attribute principle, write original example |
| Meet Easywurld | 7 intros | Rotate format and angle |

Suggested weekly timing:

- **Sunday:** verify trends, approve scripts, batch record/edit, design statics.
- **Daily:** assemble the 11 posts and 2 stories, adapt captions, QA, schedule only approved assets.
- **Saturday/Sunday:** reply, review series metrics, prepare next batch.

This is a heavy cadence. Use templates, batch generation and a shared asset library. If a slot fails QA, hold it rather than publishing unreviewed AI. Do not stack catch-up posts into a spam burst.

## 6. QA gate per placement

Before a placement moves from Draft to Scheduled:

- [ ] Facts, price, offer and sample labels checked.
- [ ] Trend verification complete, or live-trend wording removed.
- [ ] Approved likeness/voice or non-avatar fallback.
- [ ] Captions, pronunciation, crop and disclosure checked.
- [ ] One CTA and destination tested.
- [ ] Watched/read on a phone; human approval recorded.

Statuses: Draft → Script approved → Asset produced → QA approved → Scheduled → Published → Reviewed.

## 7. Measurement

Review by series after seven days:

- Saves/shares for teaching and copy posts.
- Watch time/completion for talking heads and demos.
- Profile visits and WhatsApp keyword enquiries.
- Qualified project briefs and confirmed pack sales.
- Meme shares without attracting the wrong audience.

Keep the 10/day test, but change hooks, formats and angles based on evidence. Do not declare a winner from one post. Do not invent month-end results.


## Psychology layer


Every post in this calendar carries exactly one persuasion principle. Not as a trick — as a discipline. If the principle only works when we exaggerate, we drop the principle and keep the honest version.

**Rule:** one principle per post, named in the brief and in the CSV (`Psychology move`). The copy must still be useful if the reader never buys anything.

---

## 1. The twelve principles

| Key | Principle | What it does | Where it appears | Guardrail |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `cognitive-ease` | **Cognitive ease** — *Kahneman, Thinking, Fast and Slow (2011)* | Easy-to-read ideas feel truer and safer | Short sentences, one idea per slide, wide spacing | Never use simplicity to hide a limitation |
| `loss-aversion` | **Loss aversion** — *Kahneman & Tversky, Prospect Theory (1979)* | People move faster to stop a loss than to chase a gain | "This is what the unanswered message costs you" | No fake countdowns or invented scarcity |
| `curiosity-gap` | **Curiosity gap** — *Loewenstein (1994)* | A specific open question pulls attention forward | Myth claims, copy breakdowns, Operator cold lines | Close the loop in the same post |
| `specificity` | **Specificity** — *Heath & Heath, Made to Stick (2007)* | Numbers, names and dates read as evidence | Niche plans, dated trend teardowns | Only numbers we can defend |
| `social-proof` | **Honest social proof** — *Cialdini, Influence (1984)* | Behaviour follows behaviour | Process posts, questions owners ask, labelled samples | No invented clients, testimonials or results |
| `reciprocity` | **Reciprocity** — *Cialdini (1984)* | Give the structure before asking | Free checklists, workflows, slide copy | The post must be useful alone |
| `authority-restraint` | **Authority through restraint** — *Cialdini (1984)* | Calm, sourced, unhurried statements read as authority | The Operator slot, myth verdicts | No claimed credentials or awards |
| `anchoring` | **Anchoring** — *Tversky & Kahneman (1974)* | The first number sets the frame | Offer carousels: contents → price → boundary | No fake "was ₦X" pricing |
| `peak-end` | **Peak-end rule** — *Kahneman (1999)* | People remember the strongest and the last moment | 22:00 Operator close, meme punchlines | The last line must be true and useful |
| `mere-exposure` | **Mere exposure** — *Zajonc (1968)* | Familiar shapes become liked shapes | `Meet Easywurld` repetition, fixed frames, fixed voice | Repeat the format, not the sentence |
| `identity` | **Identity and in-group** — *Berger, Contagious (2013)* | People share what says something about them | Scene-led memes | Never punch down at customers or staff |
| `objection-relief` | **Objection relief** — *Cialdini (1984); Rackham, SPIN Selling (1988)* | Name the doubt before the buyer does | Offer Spotlight B | Answer honestly, including "no" |

| S10 Meet Easywurld | Mere exposure | Honest social proof |
| S11 One Last Thought (Operator) | Authority through restraint | Peak-end |
| Stories A (poll) | Commitment — *Cialdini (1984)* | Cognitive ease |
| Stories B (behind the desk) | Mere exposure | Curiosity gap |
| LinkedIn pulls | Specificity | Authority through restraint |

The builder alternates primary and secondary by day number, so the month does not lean on one lever.

## 3. The five-line skeleton every post follows

1. **Interrupt** — a flat, specific first line that stops the scroll (curiosity gap or loss aversion).
2. **Name the real problem** — in the reader's words, not ours.
3. **Give the receipt** — one checkable detail: a dated source, a pack contents list, a step order.
4. **State the limit** — what this does not do (objection relief, authority through restraint).
5. **One ask** — the smallest next step.

Posts that cannot fill line 3 do not get published. That rule kills most inflated content before it starts.

## 4. Applied examples

**Myth Court — "posting every day guarantees growth"**
- Interrupt: *"Posting every day guarantees growth. No."*
- Problem: frequency is being used to avoid making a decision.
- Receipt: one week of series posts vs a previous week, measured on saves and enquiries.
- Limit: this does not fix an unclear offer.
- Ask: save the test.

**Offer Spotlight A — PLAYBOOK ₦5,000**
- Interrupt: *"The price is the easy part. The contents are the argument."*
- Problem: buyers cannot see what they are paying for.
- Receipt: the four named deliverables, the exact price, the DIY boundary.
- Limit: not custom work, no guaranteed results.
- Ask: message the keyword.

**Operator — 22:00**
- Interrupt: one flat, surprising sentence.
- Turn: the real mechanism.
- Close: a line worth repeating.
- Silence on the last frame.

## 5. What is banned

- Manufactured urgency, fake scarcity, "only 2 slots left".
- Invented testimonials, revenue, follower counts or client names.
- Borrowed lifestyle photos implying wealth we do not have.
- Fear framing about customers or competitors.
- Dark patterns in the CTA (pre-ticked boxes, fake chat screenshots).
- Any principle used to make a false claim land harder.

## 6. Measurement tells us whether the psychology worked

After seven days, compare per series: saves (reciprocity, specificity), shares (identity), sticker taps (commitment), keyword enquiries (anchoring, objection relief), comment quality (curiosity gap). Change one lever a week. A principle is only validated by behaviour, not by how clever the line felt.

> Sources are books and papers, cited by author and year. No framework here depends on a claim we cannot point to.

## 7. How this file drives the build

This is not a reference document that sits beside the calendar. It is the input that shapes every post.

| Field | Written by | Where you see it |
|---|---|---|
| `psychology.principles[]` | this file | `marketing/series-plan.json` → the twelve principles, their source and their guardrail |
| `psychology.seriesMap` | this file | the builder assigns a primary/secondary principle per series, alternating by day so the month does not lean on one lever |
| `psych.name`, `psych.use`, `psych.guard` | generated | every post in `content-plan.json`, every brief in `marketing/briefs/`, the `Psychology move` column in the CSV, the post detail in the studio |
| `Where it shows up here` | generated | the line in each brief that names the exact sentence or structural choice carrying the principle |

If you edit a principle or a source here, change it in `series-plan.json → psychology` too, then run `npm run content:build`. Do not edit the generated files.

## 8. Re-balancing after week one

The month is tagged, not locked. After seven days:

1. Export `marketing/MEASUREMENT.csv` with real numbers.
2. Score each series on **saves** (reciprocity, specificity), **shares** (identity), **sticker taps** (commitment), **keyword enquiries** (anchoring, objection relief) and **comment quality** (curiosity gap).
3. Change **one lever per series per week**: the hook, the length, or the ask. Never three at once, or you learn nothing.
4. If a principle is consistently underperforming on a series, swap its primary to the secondary and run the next week as a test.
5. Keep the 22:00 Operator slot for a full three weeks before judging it. The peak-end effect needs repetition to show up in follows.

> A principle is validated by behaviour, not by how clever the line felt when you wrote it.

**2026-11-07 · Saturday · 22:00 WAT · One Last Thought · AI talking head**

- **Pillar:** Trust
- **Objective:** Close the day with one calm, certain line from the faceless Operator persona. Builds familiarity, authority and the 22:00 return habit.
- **Single CTA:** Save this and clear five tonight.
- **Target length:** 18–24s
- **Status:** Draft — not scheduled
- **Expected asset:** `assets/video-ready/EW-D06-S11.mp4 (record) or assets/fallbacks/EW-D06-S11.jpg (poster)`
- **Destination to verify:** https://website-builder-portfolio.vercel.app/about
- **Contact:** 0905 069 0837

- **Psychology move:** Peak-end rule — People remember the strongest moment and the last one. So end the day with the sharpest line.
- **Where it shows up here:** a flat first line, a slow turn and a last line the reader can repeat tomorrow.
- **Guard:** The last line must be true and actionable, not just a punchline.

### Hook / first frame

> Every unanswered message is a price you already agreed to pay.

### Exact spoken script

> Every unanswered message is a price you already agreed to pay. You did the advertising, then let the reply die in a list you never open. Answer five a day. The list is the calendar. Save this and clear five tonight.

### Voiceover script — plain Nigerian English

This is what the voice says. `[pause]` means let the idea land for about a second. Read the words exactly as written; do not formalise them.

> Every unanswered message is a price you already agreed to pay. [pause] You did the advertising, then let the reply die in a list you never open. Referrals dry up, and the only new customer this month is your cousin. [pause] Answer five a day. The list is the calendar. We fight this every day at Easywurld, and we are honest about it: we cannot win it alone. No wahala. Save this and clear five tonight.

### Burned-in caption chunks

Already timed and rendered into the finished MP4. Fix a word here and re-run `python marketing/build-video.py --only ${p.id}`.

2. agreed to pay

- 2–8s: the turn.

**2026-11-08 · Sunday · 08:30 WAT · Marketing Myth Court · AI talking head**

But we cannot win it alone. Run this small test this week. State the review boundary before starting and send a written scope for extra work. Take it one step at a time. Your yes is the turning point. Keep the useful part. Drop the absolute.

## EW-D08-S02 · Myth Court: Discounts always increase sales.

**2026-11-09 · Monday · 08:30 WAT · Marketing Myth Court · AI talking head**

- **Pillar:** Trust
- **Objective:** Replace absolute marketing advice with a verdict and a small test.
- **Single CTA:** Save the test and run it on your own account.
- **Target length:** 35–50s
- **Status:** Draft — not scheduled
- **Expected asset:** `assets/video-ready/EW-D08-S02.mp4 (record) or assets/fallbacks/EW-D08-S02.jpg (poster)`
- **Destination to verify:** https://website-builder-portfolio.vercel.app/about
- **Contact:** 0905 069 0837

- **Psychology move:** Loss aversion — People move faster to stop a loss than to chase a gain. Name the cost of waiting, without inventing urgency.
- **Where it shows up here:** the verdict named early, then a test the reader can run: “what the absolute advice is costing you”.
- **Guard:** No fake countdowns, no invented scarcity. The loss must be real and checkable.

### Hook / first frame

> Marketing myth: Discounts always increase sales.

### Exact spoken script

> Marketing myth: Discounts always increase sales Verdict: It depends. A discount can attract price-sensitive buyers and reduce margin. It can also train customers to wait. Test whether the offer is clear before reducing price. Test it: Run one non-discount offer post and compare qualified enquiries. That is Myth Court: keep the useful part, drop the absolute.

### Voiceover script — plain Nigerian English

This is what the voice says. `[pause]` means let the idea land for about a second. Read the words exactly as written; do not formalise them.

> Let us put one piece of advice on trial. "Discounts always increase sales." [pause] My verdict? It depends. A discount can attract price-sensitive buyers and reduce margin. It can also train customers to wait. [pause] People see "DM for price" and just pass, money in hand. That is the fight Easywurld picks every day. But we cannot win it alone. Run this small test this week. Run one non-discount offer post and compare qualified messages. Your yes is the turning point. Keep the useful part. Drop the absolute.

### Burned-in caption chunks

Already timed and rendered into the finished MP4. Fix a word here and re-run `python marketing/build-video.py --only ${p.id}`.

1. Let us put one piece of advice on trial
2. Discounts always increase sales my verdict? It depends
3. A discount can attract price-sensitive buyers and reduce margin
4. It can also train customers to wait

### Exact spoken script

> “We will go viral” is not a plan. It is a lottery ticket with a caption. Twelve useful posts a day beats one lucky one you cannot repeat. Build the repeatable thing. Save this for the next strategy meeting.

### Voiceover script — plain Nigerian English

This is what the voice says. `[pause]` means let the idea land for about a second. Read the words exactly as written; do not formalise them.

> “We will go viral” is not a plan. It is a lottery ticket with a caption. [pause] Twelve useful posts a day beats one lucky one you cannot repeat. Somebody types your own business name into Google and finds nothing. Then they find somebody else. [pause] Build the repeatable thing. We fight this every day at Easywurld, and we are honest about it: we cannot win it alone. Take it one step at a time. Save this for the next strategy meeting.

> → Only then: a reviewed proposal draft
>
> The part I will not automate is the check. A machine can write a reply. It should not be allowed to promise a price, a date or a result on my behalf.
>
> That boundary is the product. Everything else is convenience.
>
> Labelled concept work — a sample build, not a client result.
>
> Where would you keep a human in the loop in your own business?

> Myth I keep hearing: "More posts will fix an unclear offer."

> Volume can amplify confusion. The offer sentence, proof and next step need to be clear before scaling content.
